dedupe_keys.name: feijao dam i brumadinho tailings dam failure expert panel report on technical causes 2019

description: This case study is the expert panel investigation of the 25 January 2019 failure of tailings dam B-I at Vale S.A.'s Córrego do Feijão iron ore mine near Brumadinho, Minas Gerais, Brazil. The report read on 2026-09-26, dated 12 December 2019, says the slope failed in under 10 seconds and 9.7 million cubic metres, about 75 percent of the stored tailings, flowed out in under five minutes by flow (static) liquefaction, with no signs of distress in monitoring by survey monuments, inclinometers, ground radar and piezometers, while satellite analysis later showed slow deformations under 36 mm a year. It attributes the conditions for failure to a steep upstream-raised dam, a high internal water level, weak fine tailings and brittle, bonded iron-rich tailings, and examines possible small triggers. The panel of four geotechnical experts chaired by Peter K. Robertson was commissioned by Vale, and the report is a free PDF download (81 pages) with appendices and a video on the panel website; no licence is stated. Caveats: the panel did not assess corporate or personal responsibility. For simulation it gives a documented failure mechanism, monitoring record and runout volume to test tailings dam failure, early warning and downstream cascade models. Related catalogue records include the Mount Polley tailings breach review and the tailings dam breach runout characteristics data.
